assumptions: Both hands are on the bar and both knees are on the floor, so laterality is bilateral.
Joint actions describe the concentric return phase, where the bar is pulled back toward the knees.
The elbows stay roughly extended throughout, so the elbow is a stabilizer and not a primary mover.
The return is driven by glenohumeral extension, hip flexion and slight lumbar flexion, while the trunk resists extension.
The bar rolls on the floor with the hands and knees fixed in contact, so the chain is treated as closed.
classification_reasons: The kneeling barbell rollout is clear from the text and both frames: hands on a barbell, knees on the floor, and the bar rolled forward then pulled back.
The concentric return phase can be represented with the available vocabulary as glenohumeral extension, lumbar flexion and hip flexion, with anti-extension trunk demand.

instructions: Hold an Olympic barbell loaded with 5-10lbs on each side and kneel on the floor.
Now place the barbell on the floor in front of you so that you are on all your hands and knees (as in a kneeling push up position). This will be your starting position.

Slowly roll the barbell straight forward, stretching your body into a straight position. Tip: Go down as far as you can without touching the floor with your body. Breathe in during this portion of the movement.
After a second pause at the stretched position, start pulling yourself back to the starting position as you breathe out. Tip: Go slowly and keep your abs tight at all times.
